c.tagline: Australia's tropical Top End capital and the gateway to Kakadu and Litchfield.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered; phone or app bookings add a small booking fee and airport pickups carry a surcharge. Ride-hailing apps are widely used as an alternative.

emergency.note: 000 is the primary emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 112 also works from any mobile and 106 is the text-based line for the deaf or speech-impaired.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Late-night Mitchell Street can get rowdy with alcohol-fuelled trouble, and never swim in the sea or estuaries — crocodiles year-round and box jellyfish roughly October to May.

hood_desc: The compact, walkable city centre around the Smith Street Mall, Mitchell Street's bars and the Esplanade; best for first-timers who want dining, nightlife and the harbour all within a few blocks.

A modern, purpose-built leisure precinct with a wave lagoon and safe swimming pool, waterside restaurants and apartment hotels, linked to the CBD by a footbridge and lift; suits families and travellers who want the water on their doorstep.

An upmarket marina enclave five minutes from the centre, ringed by waterfront restaurants and a lock-gated harbour, and the departure point for the Mandorah ferry; a short walk from the famous Mindil Beach Sunset Markets and the Botanic Gardens.

A leafy inner suburb about 4 km from the CBD known for its relaxed cafe strip and the popular Saturday Parap Village Markets; suits travellers wanting a quieter, local base with easy access to the city.

A calm residential bayside suburb with sailing and racing clubs, quiet beaches and some of Darwin's best sunset spots, near the Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory; good for a slow-paced, local stay.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Darwinbus services generally run from around 6:00 AM to 7:30 PM on weekdays with reduced weekend and public-holiday timetables; there is no late-night network, so taxis or ride apps cover the evenings.
transit.note: Darwin has no train, tram or ferry commuter network within the city; the Darwinbus public bus network is the only public transport, radiating from the Darwin Bus Interchange on Harry Chan Avenue in the CBD.
transit.pay: Tap on with a rechargeable Tap and Ride card or pay cash to the driver; a standard adult single is a flat AUD 3 (about US$2) valid for 3 hours of transfers, and children, seniors and concession holders travel free. Cards are sold and topped up at the Bus Interchange and selected agents.

bus: Greyhound & long-distance coaches to Katherine, Alice Springs and beyond
train: The Ghan (long-distance rail to Katherine, Alice Springs and Adelaide)

transit.m: Darwin Airport Shuttle to city hotels (~20-30 min, door-to-door)
Darwinbus public route to the city (limited, ~30-40 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving around 10% for excellent service at restaurants is appreciated but never obligatory.
